papers.title: ReAlign: Reward-Guided Preference Alignment for Generative Re-Ranking
papers.summary: Re-ranking should turn an upstream candidate set into the list with the highest user utility, but two-stage generator-evaluator methods split generation from evaluation, so the generator never sees the listwise utility signal. Scoring methods often stay inside the upstream order and never really search the space of permutations. Coupling a decomposable listwise reward model with a candidate-aware autoregressive generator splits the reward by position, models user exposure with a survival function, and estimates heterogeneous engagement such as likes and follows with per-objective heads. The generator is first trained on logged exposure lists, then aligned with within-pool standardized rewards on both the distribution and the ranking. On KuaiRand, NDCG rises from 0.8450 with the strongest baseline, CAVE, to 0.8551. On Avito it rises from 0.7372 to 0.7476. ==Listwise utility steers permutation search toward real engagement only when it is fed back into generation itself==.
papers.abstract: Re-ranking refines the upstream ranked list to maximize listwise user utility. Existing two-stage generator-evaluator methods decouple list generation from list evaluation, leaving the generator without direct access to the listwise utility signal, while scoring-based one-stage methods score items under a fixed upstream permutation context without explicitly searching the permutation space. We propose \textbf{ReAlign}, a reward-guided preference alignment framework that couples a listwise reward model with a candidate-aware autoregressive generator. The reward model decomposes the listwise reward into position-wise contributions, modeling user exposure through a survival-based exposure module and item value through per-objective heads for heterogeneous engagement signals. The generator is trained in two stages: supervised pre-training on logged exposure lists to establish a relevance prior, followed by reward-guided post-training that aligns the generator with the reward model through complementary distribution and ranking alignment over within-pool standardized rewards. Extensive offline experiments show that ReAlign consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines.

scenario: Today's generative track has a single paper, and it focuses on generative re-ranking at the last stage of recommendation. The upstream ranker has already produced a short list; the hard part is finding a higher-utility order in a factorial space of permutations, while users browse position by position and engagement objectives such as likes and follows are not just one signal. Existing two-stage methods split generation from evaluation, so the generator never sees the listwise reward, and scoring methods rarely search the permutation space at all. Coupling a decomposable listwise reward with an autoregressive generator, first pre-training on logged exposure lists and then aligning the policy with the reward, beats strong baselines on two public benchmarks offline. Today's question is whether generative re-ranking can write list utility into the generation process itself, rather than scoring a list only after it has been produced.
